summary: The V2 permission migration is sound: the emitted permissions schema was verified against OpenCode V2's official documentation, the new YAML serializer branch is injection-safe, and the honest verification limits match the spec; one pre-existing, spec-sanctioned trust-boundary gap (read-only roles never deny shell/execute) is reported as advisory.

findings.summary: Read-only roles deny only the edit and subagent actions, leaving shell and execute at the V2 default allow policy, so the 'read-only' guarantee of reviewer roles is enforced only against the edit tool and can be bypassed by any shell command.
findings.evidence: Rendered read roles (e.g. dist/opencode/agents/factory-security-reviewer.md lines 4-6) emit exactly [{action: edit, resource: *, effect: deny}, {action: subagent, resource: *, effect: deny}] with no shell or execute rule. OpenCode V2's permissions doc (https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/permissions) gives every agent the base policy {action: *, resource: *, effect: allow} and warns that 'shell runs with the host user's filesystem, process, and network authority'. A reviewer agent (factory-security-reviewer, factory-code-standards, factory-review-judge) consumes attacker-controlled repo content, so a prompt injection can direct it to mutate the reviewed tree via shell, defeating the intent the docs state ('Read-only roles deny edit', adapters/opencode/harness.md). This is NOT a regression introduced by this change (the old V1 config also left bash undenied), FR-002 defines the required restrictions as exactly edit+subagent, and the plan explicitly forbids broadening policy, so spec conformance is met; reported at the design-guidance ceiling under ENG-25 (enforce authorisation at trusted boundaries) as an advisory trust-boundary gap for the maintainer.
findings.fix: Consider adding { "action": "shell", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" } (and/or execute) to read-access rules in a follow-up once confirmed that reviewer roles need no shell commands; alternatively document in harness.md that read-only protection covers the edit tool only.
